finiteE4Decisions.title: Keep proof and sealed schema equality JSON-type-sensitive
finiteE4Decisions.finding: Python equality accepts True == 1, also inside dictionaries/lists. Orchestration can therefore commit STATE_VERIFIED with differently typed observation bytes. const/enum have the same coercion before schema type validation (integer schema with const true admits integer 1). Existing effect projection already compares canonical digests correctly.
finiteE4Decisions.replacement: Reuse existing canonical JSON equality semantics for observed/expected proof and const/enum membership; preserve result/state contracts and the documented schema subset. No new verification framework.
finiteE4Decisions.risk: False success/admission for differently typed provider evidence. Source-level finding, not an observed household incident.
finiteE4Decisions.verificationRequired: During E4 only: focused boolean/integer/nested mismatch checks plus existing success and schema regression routes. No test or provider execution in this review.

finiteE4Decisions.title: Give existing tool/provider boundaries one owner of protocol guidance and deadlines
finiteE4Decisions.finding: Channel-neutral conversation embeds Home Assistant REST return_response/body protocol instructions. ConversationToolPreparation and ToolRequest separately special-case the same research.public_sources 125-second timeout. Protocol/deadline ownership is duplicated in general turn/orchestration boundaries.
finiteE4Decisions.replacement: Move the existing HA protocol paragraph to existing provider tool guidance and define the admitted timeout bound once in the existing preparation/request translation. Preserve conversation routing, tool names, durable budgets and wire behavior. No provider framework or whole-module rewrite.
finiteE4Decisions.risk: Adapter protocol fixes or deadline changes can drift across validators and prompt. Token/cost benefit unmeasured.
finiteE4Decisions.verificationRequired: Existing HA preparation/guidance and current-state read plus durable research admission; preserve behavior before claiming simplification. E4.3 measures usage only when relevant; no optimization trial now.

finiteE4Decisions.title: Move saved-artifact target validation to its neutral boundary
finiteE4Decisions.finding: Pure application draft/release construction imports operations.component_evaluation for a host-resolved saved-artifact target validator. This reverses the declared application import boundary and loads the operational evaluator module on a pure artifact construction path.
finiteE4Decisions.replacement: Move the existing pure closed-shape validator into an appropriate existing application/contract boundary; application and operations consume the same definition. Preserve exact hashes, retention and source/current-authority checks. No weakened gate, hidden-criteria change or alias back to operations.
finiteE4Decisions.risk: Evaluation implementation coupling and future duplicate target definitions; exact wire bytes must remain compatible.
finiteE4Decisions.verificationRequired: Existing saved-artifact draft/release and evaluator interface checks during E4; protected final cases remain independent.

finiteE4Decisions.title: Preserve semantic trust in MemoryAuthority context
finiteE4Decisions.finding: MemoryAuthority maps inferred/legacy facts to ConfirmedFact.host_policy and copies value unchanged. Unlike Hindsight it does not add semantic_trust consumed by the model's uncertainty qualifier. RecalledFact retains original trust but does not supply that model-visible qualifier. Direct current constructors found are legacy trial and isolated component evaluation; ordinary Hindsight already preserves semantic_trust. No claim that all household responses lose uncertainty.
finiteE4Decisions.replacement: Preserve original semantic trust in the existing context/value representation consistently with Hindsight, or filter unsupported inferred facts at this adapter. Keep source provenance, audience and current ConfirmedFact wire enum; any incompatible enum change needs versioned transition.
finiteE4Decisions.risk: Legacy/evaluation or future MemoryAuthority consumer can omit intended uncertainty qualifier. Scope is this adapter boundary, not a proven ordinary Hindsight runtime failure.
finiteE4Decisions.verificationRequired: Focused MemoryAuthority-to-model inferred/legacy/direct context cases and retained Hindsight behavior during E4; no new memory or private/protected evaluation reads.

finiteE4Decisions.title: Bind default identity JSON to package/install ownership
finiteE4Decisions.finding: Default pack/trust loaders read JSON beside application modules. Explicit setuptools package-data lists voice/model/API resources but not application/*.json. Current Docker source COPY supplies bytes separately and does not prove wheel resource completeness. No wheel failure executed.
finiteE4Decisions.replacement: E3.3 confirms actual build/install ownership; E4.4 explicitly packages the two exact signed resources or documents/enforces the chosen non-wheel source delivery contract. Keep pack and public trust bytes unchanged.
finiteE4Decisions.risk: Isolated installed-package default identity can fail despite working source checkout/Docker; no production outage asserted.
finiteE4Decisions.verificationRequired: One package-resource/identity-load interface check within existing E3.3/E4.4 install route; no blanket image rebuild or private identity change.
